title: Tests that pass or fail on clock speed become outcome checks, then CI caps return to measured
why: Owner, Nov 1 18:44 CST: "we have a step regarding fixing CI that eliminates time limits and instead ensures outcomes based testing". No step did this (searched c34, c39, c128, test-ci-standard, tci-7, tci-8; gap found by tci-12). Generous job caps are a stopgap until it lands (decision ci-job-caps).
note: In q_max, banchi, degen, joyous, mailaudit and ios-adblock (home through its own lane): find tests that pass or fail on wall-clock speed (real sleeps, fixed timeouts that assert speed, runner-speed caps inside tests) and replace each with an outcome check (fake clock, wait for a condition), per decision test-strategy-reset. Then return each repo's job caps to measured figures, closing the ci-job-caps stopgap. Done check: a per-repo list of time-pinned tests found, each replaced or recorded as a debt, and caps re-measured. Port: yes, every repo with CI. Ready. Part 1 in draft PR #1026 (batch runner 7), Nov 1 21:08 CST: finder lint/find_time_pinned.py and docs/plans/time-pinned-tests.md with per-repo counts and file lists. Found: q_max 326, banchi 357, degen 1346, joyous 41, mailaudit 319, ios-adblock 1; home unscanned (held). Part 2, the per-repo lanes, starts after #1026 merges. Part 2 steps, one per repo: time-pinned-qmax, -banchi, -degen, -joyous, -mailaudit, -ios-adblock, -cs (claude-settings: 238). home: none until it is scanned.
